status: frozen before downloading regional antecedent weather or fitting predictive models
inference: predictive out of sample, not causal and not an operational forecast
research_question: Could the August 2026 thermal fire activity detected in Tolima have been anticipated from conditions known by 31 July, using prior August seasons in Tolima and seven pre specified neighbouring departments?

temporal_design.historical_validation: leave one complete standard processing season out from 2012 through 2025. The training set for each historical fold contains only the remaining standard processing seasons and never includes 2026. All eight departments of the held out season remain together.

outcomes.primary: VIIRS Suomi NPP total August detections assigned by point containment to department
outcomes.secondary: number of one kilometre cells with at least one VIIRS Suomi NPP August detection
outcomes.sensitivity: VIIRS Suomi NPP nominal or high confidence August detections

antecedent_moisture.source: CHIRPS v3 monthly global cloud optimised GeoTIFF
antecedent_moisture.coverage: May through July of each outcome season from 2012 through 2026
antecedent_moisture.rule: monthly precipitation values are spatially aggregated by department from pixel centres and all source months end no later than July

fuel_and_landscape.source: MapBiomas Colombia collection 3 departmental annual statistics
fuel_and_landscape.temporal_rule: use year t minus 1 for outcome year t. For 2025 and 2026 carry 2024 and flag the carry forward

department_baseline.source: pre specified department identities and geodesic area from GeoBoundaries
department_baseline.purpose: account for time invariant spatial differences in detection opportunity and landscape extent. A log area offset is deliberately excluded because it is exactly collinear with a full set of department fixed effects.

diagnostic_only_predictors.source: ERA5 Land August atmospheric danger metrics
diagnostic_only_predictors.rule: excluded from anticipation models because they are not fully known by 31 July

modelling.baseline: department historical mean calculated within each training set
modelling.primary_candidate: negative binomial count model with department fixed effects
modelling.fallback: Poisson count model with season clustered robust variance if negative binomial estimation is not stable
modelling.selection_rule: no automatic selection, no selection by significance and one representative per correlated physical block

frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.selection_status: fixed after predictor collinearity diagnosis and before any predictive model fitting or performance result
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.baseline: within training set department historical mean
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.primary: negative binomial count model with May through July CHIRPS precipitation, lagged agricultural fraction and department fixed effects
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.fallback: Poisson count model with the same terms only if the negative binomial model fails a documented convergence or stability check
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.physical_sensitivity: replace May through July precipitation with July precipitation, never include both because their Pearson correlation is 0.814 in the assembled panel
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.coverage_sensitivity: replace lagged agricultural fraction with lagged natural non forest fraction, never include forest and agricultural fractions together because their Pearson correlation is minus 0.934 in the assembled panel
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.coverage_basis_reason: agricultural fraction is the primary territorial proxy because it is directly interpretable as managed land extent. It is a predictive feature and not evidence that agriculture caused any ignition.
frozen_model_set_2026_09_10.scaling_rule: within every training fold, continuous time varying predictors are centred on the training median and divided by the training interquartile range. Held out rows use the corresponding training constants.

evaluation.required_comparison: all expanded models must be compared with the within training set department historical mean baseline
evaluation.2026_reporting: report prediction trained on 2012 through 2025, uncertainty interval if estimable, and position in the distribution of leave one season out historical errors

falsification_checks: repeat primary outcome using nominal or high confidence detections
repeat after excluding Cundinamarca because standard processing type labels show a higher non vegetation fraction
compare all eight departments in 2026 to assess whether processing level change creates a regional shift
repeat using precipitation rather than July soil water as antecedent moisture representative
repeat without 2025 and 2026 carried forward land cover values
re execute after August 2026 standard processing is available
interpretation_limits: A good model would predict satellite detected activity, not physical fire occurrence or damage.
A predictive association does not identify ignition cause or a causal effect of rainfall, soil moisture or land cover.
The time almost real versus standard processing difference remains a measurement limitation until direct calibration is possible.

technical_amendment_2026_09_10.change: The raw antecedent retrieval is restricted from December 2011 through July 2026 to May through July of each outcome season.
technical_amendment_2026_09_10.reason: The frozen candidate features are July mean soil water and precipitation accumulated over 30 or 90 days before 31 July. May through July covers all primary and sensitivity windows. The earlier expanded coverage would consume data outside every pre specified feature.
technical_amendment_2026_09_10.timing: The amendment follows a successful one day access audit and precedes any analytical regional antecedent feature or model result.
technical_amendment_2026_09_10.effect_on_inference: The raw temporal coverage is reduced without changing cutoff, outcome, validation or model rules.

source_amendment_2026_09_10.change: CHIRPS v3 monthly precipitation replaces ERA5 Land soil water as the antecedent physical predictor in the current regional panel.
source_amendment_2026_09_10.reason: The ERA5 Land regional one day access audit passed, but a three year request was rejected for size and a complete month did not return data or an error within the predeclared five minute waiting limit. CHIRPS v3 monthly access, GeoTIFF structure and local pixel decoding passed the audit.
source_amendment_2026_09_10.new_features: July monthly precipitation and the May through July total. The latter is 92 days, not an exact 90 day rolling accumulation, and is named accordingly.
source_amendment_2026_09_10.interpretation_limit: Precipitation is not treated as a substitute for soil moisture. The study will report that soil moisture could not be included within the available retrieval timeline.
